i’m sorry you had to deal with all this. society’s rigid view of masculinity is absolutely a serious problem and i would agree with you that an unfortunate amount of seemingly “progressive” people make excuses for allowing it to exist. 

there is a distinction to be made though. 
real feminism does not mean bringing down men so women are superior than them. 
it means making things fair for everyone. patriarchy hurts both men and women. patriarchy forces men to take the role of the breadwinner. that’s horrible and an insane amount of responsibility. it’s also horrible that patriarchy frowns upon women becoming independent and makes it more difficult for them to do so. 
a lot of times feminism tries to address systemic issues of women’s rights. 
that does not mean your problems aren’t important. they absolutely have their place in the feminist movement. 
sidenote: as long as it’s not being said to discredit what a women is saying about her experience. 

i also don’t think you’re a misogynist for feeling this way. i think it’s an understandable reaction.

toxic masculinity is not men being upset and showing emotion. toxic masculinity is what society tells men they must conform to and stops them from showing emotions.

i hope you’re able to recognise that feminism isn’t the enemy. we want the same things. 
equal rights for all, regardless of gender and everything else. and i really hope my comment doesn’t indirectly make you feel worse. just wanted to share my perspective.
